study <- "experiments/estimate_intrinsic_m_v032"
result_dir <- file.path(study, "main_summary")
status <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(result_dir, "status.json"))
stopifnot(isTRUE(status$complete), status$completed_method_runs == 180)
design <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(study, "design.json"), simplifyVector = TRUE)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, out.width = "100%")

## Question

Can MPCurve recover the number of latent sample orderings when the true
number is three, four, or five? We compare **adaptive empirical Bayes (EB)**
with **a fixed uniform ordering prior and forward selection**, using the
same simulated datasets for both methods.

## Simulation design

Each dataset has **300 samples and 60 features**. Features belong to equally
sized groups following **3, 4, or 5 independent orderings**, giving 20, 15,
or 12 features per ordering. For sample $i$ and feature $j$,

$$X_{ij}=f_j(t_{i,z_j})+\epsilon_{ij},$$

where $z_j$ identifies the generating ordering, latent positions are
independent Uniform$(0,1)$ draws, and $f_j$ is a smooth monotone curve.
Each curve is a random weighted combination of monotone basis functions,
with its direction chosen to be increasing or decreasing. Under the parameters
used here, most resulting trajectories have mild curvature and are close to
linear. Each noiseless feature is
centered and scaled to sample variance one before independent Gaussian
noise is added.

The variance signal-to-noise ratio is **1, 4, or 16**, corresponding to
noise standard deviations of 1, 0.5, or 0.25. There are **10 independent
datasets for each of the nine conditions**, or **90 datasets in total**.
Separate pilot datasets were used to check the implementation and runtime;
they are excluded from these results.

### Simulated trajectories and observations

The figures below show **replicate 1 from every condition**. Each row is a
true ordering and each column is an SNR setting. For the first three features
in each group, solid lines show the noiseless signal and points show all 300
noisy observations, plotted against that group's true latent positions.
All panels use the same axis scales. Conditions use independent datasets,
so both the generating curves and noise realizations differ across columns.

```{r estimate-m-design-three, fig.alt="True M equals 3: three ordering rows and three SNR columns, showing noiseless trajectories and noisy observations."}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(result_dir, "design_M3.png")))
```

## Methods

Both methods use MPCurver **0.3.2**, CAVI, **50 grid positions**, a second-order
random-walk prior with `ridge = 0`, adaptive cell-position priors, and estimated
feature-specific noise and smoothness. Initialization clusters features using
absolute Spearman correlation and single linkage, then uses Isomap within
each group. A singleton group is initialized by ranking its feature.

- **Adaptive EB:** fit eight candidate orderings with adaptive ordering-assignment
  weights.
- **Uniform + forward:** fix the ordering prior to $1/M$, start at $M=1$,
  and fit successively larger $M$, up to eight. Accept a candidate only when
  its converged, soft-assignment ELBO at temperature one exceeds the preceding
  candidate's score. Stop at the first non-improvement.

For both methods, the estimated **effective M** counts orderings whose mean
posterior feature-assignment probability exceeds $10^{-12}$. Unused ordering
slots are excluded. For adaptive EB, these mean probabilities equal the fitted
assignment-prior weights.

Each candidate has one initialization. Partition fits use a temperature
schedule from five to one, followed by refinement at temperature one.
Fitting stops when the absolute ELBO change divided by $N D$ is below
$10^{-6}$, subject to the algorithm's numerical nondecrease check and
completion of annealing. Continuation preserves the current fit. Candidates that remain unconverged after the declared
10,000-sweep limit are recorded as unresolved, including forward searches
whose next comparison cannot be completed.

## Recovery of M

Exact recovery, underestimation, overestimation, and unresolved outcomes use
all 10 planned repeats as their denominator. Error bars are 95% Wilson
intervals. The methods are assessed against the generating truth; their
ELBO values are not compared against each other.

Adaptive EB recovers the true effective M in **`r sum(summary$exact[summary$method == "adaptive"])` of 90 datasets**;
uniform + forward does so in **`r sum(summary$exact[summary$method == "forward"])` of 90 datasets**.

```{r estimate-m-recovery}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(result_dir, "exact_recovery.png")))
```

```{r estimate-m-table}
table <- summary[, c("true_M", "snr", "method", "exact", "under", "over", "failed")]
names(table) <- c("True M", "SNR", "Method", "Exact", "Under", "Over", "Unresolved")
table$Method <- ifelse(table$Method == "adaptive", "Adaptive EB", "Uniform + forward")
knitr::kable(table, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Counts out of 10 datasets per condition and method.")
```

```{r estimate-m-distribution}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(result_dir, "estimated_M_distribution.png")))
```

## Recovery of the underlying structure

Feature-group recovery is measured by the adjusted Rand index (ARI), assigning
each feature to the ordering with the largest posterior assignment probability.
An ordering with no assigned features does not change this partition.

For ordering recovery, inferred positions are matched one-to-one to the
true orderings by absolute Spearman correlation, allowing reversal of an
axis. Unmatched true orderings contribute zero to the mean recovery score.
These structural summaries describe completed fits; unresolved rates are
reported separately above.

```{r estimate-m-structure}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(result_dir, "structural_recovery.png")))
```

## Runtime and convergence

Runtime includes initialization and every candidate and continuation used
by each method. A forward search therefore includes its rejected stopping
candidate. All workers use one CPU thread.

```{r estimate-m-runtime}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(result_dir, "runtime.png")))
```

The study completed **`r sum(runs$status == "success")` of 180 method runs**
with a converged estimate. The remaining **`r sum(runs$status != "success")`**
runs are included as unresolved outcomes in the main recovery rates.

## Summary and reproduction

Both approaches recover the effective number of orderings well in this
benchmark of balanced feature groups, independent orderings, and mostly
mildly curved monotone trajectories. Uniform-prior greedy forward selection
has slightly higher recovery in these simulations: **90/90**, compared with
**87/90** for adaptive EB. The three EB errors each add one effective ordering.

The [experiment directory](https://github.com/AgueroZZ/InferOrder/tree/master/experiments/estimate_intrinsic_m_v032)
contains the fixed design and seeds, scripts, summaries, and standalone
report source. Each dataset is shared by the two methods, and saved
candidates support continuation and reproducibility.
